cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Steer the Suspicion
cards.instruction: Hide your responsibility by redirecting every new clue toward a safer explanation before anyone can connect it back to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Your shelf fell because they supplied the wrong bracket. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You fitted it upside down. Look at the arrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. That's a misleading arrow. We should photograph it for the manufacturer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You drew that arrow. I watched you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because theirs was missing. Put that in the complaint; they made us supply our own safety markings.

mechanism: A manages a shelf complaint and adjusts the evidence collection while turning both faulty installation and A own arrow into manufacturer responsibility.
confusable: Unlike correcting a repair mistake, A redirects every clue toward a safer culprit; borrowed authority does supporting work so B keeps documenting that account.
comparison: Installation markings and retrospective complaint differ from ongoing ink damage during a delivery dispute.
seedUse: D133-b bracket, upside-down fitting and self-drawn arrow; S02-b adapts the proposed evidence task as B supplies inconvenient facts.
